page.layout: One page of running text in the right column. Marginal notes in the left margin, beside the text lines they belong to. Catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: Primus Siciliæ & Italiæ Rexprimus titulum Siciliæ ac Italiæ Re-gis ufurpavit,

Tum captô Innocentio II. & ho-norificè dimissô Rogerius ab eo Ne-apoli & aliis Græcorum regionibus donatus est; ejus tamen svafu titu-lô Regis Italiæ abstinuit; contentus Regem Siciliæ, Ducem Apuliæ & Calabriæ, Principem Capuæ, Neapolis, Regna Siculū & Nea-polita-num à Normānis ad Svevos transfe-re ab bis ad An-dega-venses.Salerni, Amalfis Dominum se appel-lare. Heinricus IV. Imperator Ro-gerio III. Siciliam & Neapolin ade-mit relictis ei tantùm Ducatu Taren-tino & Comitatu Lucaniæ, qvæ tamen paulò post etiam Ducatui Svevia ad-jecit. Ultimus ex familia Ducum Svevia Rex Siciliæ & Neapolis fuit Conradinus, quem Carolus Andega-vensis decollari jussit.
Ita regnum Siciliæ & Neapolis ad familiam Andegavensem pervenit. A C.1270. Amissâ per vesperas Si-culas A. C. 1282, Siciliâ dein ceps ad Aragonios,Carolus Re-

page.notes: The first note is a sidenote beside the opening lines. The left-margin notes are "Primus Siciliæ & Italiæ Rex", "Regna Siculū ... Andegavenses" and "dein ceps ad Aragonios,". The date "A C.1270." and "A. C. 1282" are read as printed but are doubtful, so they should be checked against the scan. "relictis" is a doubtful reading of the word after "ei tantùm"; the scan looks like "reliĉtis". The line "Normānis" breaks without a visible hyphen. Last line of the page is printed "Carolus Re-", the catchword "Re-" is at the bottom right. The page is in running text with no headings.
